LATE EDITION
Fair and Clear

layers.name: dateline
layers.text: VOL. I, No. 1          TUESDAY EVENING          PRICE ONE CENT

layers.name: deck
layers.text: Letters Read From the Curves of the Font at Any Size, Witnesses Say

layers.name: column1
layers.text:
A glass lens drifted over the
front page of this paper on
Tuesday evening, and the words
beneath it grew. Each letter
kept a clean edge at every size.
No picture of the page was ever
made: the shader reads every
letter from the curves of the
font, at the size where the
glass sets it down, and so the
ink stays as sharp at five
times as it does at one. The
lens was last seen heading for
the weather report.

layers.name: column2
layers.text:
THE METHOD. Each pixel
under the glass asks where
on the page its light comes
from. Near the middle the
answer is close by, and the
page grows. Toward the rim
the glass bends harder, the
answer runs far out, and the
words crowd into a ring. The
shader asks the font how much
of that point the ink covers,
at the size that the glass
gives it, and each edge comes
out one pixel soft, be the
letter large or small.

layers.name: column3
layers.text:
WEATHER. Fair and clear,
with a lens passing over from
the west at a brisk pace.
Light winds. More glass is
expected by morning.

NOTICES. Lost, a magnifier
with a brass rim, much loved.
The finder will please return
it to the editor.

Wanted, a reader with time
to spare for very small print.
Inquire within.
